title: Watch what Trump does in Asia, not what he says
gist: Bisley argues Trump's Asia summit season (EAS in Manila, APEC in Shenzhen, third Trump–Xi bilateral) should be judged by deeds not words; the surprise of Trump's second term is the absence of hostility toward China, and a US–China 'grand bargain' would reshape the region, while a Russia–China–US 'Yalta'-style Ukraine deal is implausible.

insights.claim: Trump's intentions can only be reliably read from his actions, as his approach is instinctive, personalised and opportunistic rather than ideological or strategic.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: Fade headline rhetoric from Trump in Asia; trade on concrete actions (tariffs, deals, deployments).
insights.quote: his approach has been and will remain instinctive, personalised and opportunistic

insights.claim: After a Republican midterm 'drubbing', Trump replaced chief of staff Susie Wiles with hardline immigration architect Stephen Miller, signalling he will not moderate course.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: Expect a more combative, not more moderate, White House in the lame-duck period; policy volatility stays elevated.
insights.quote: expect a chastened Trump White House to respond to the Republican mid-term election drubbing and trim its sails

insights.claim: In his lame-duck final two years Trump will likely focus on his global legacy, though his mercurial tendencies make almost any outcome possible.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: Legacy-seeking raises odds of big headline deals (China, Ukraine) — event risk in both directions.
insights.locator: Commentators are attempting to guess where

insights.claim: The most surprising feature of Trump's second term has been the lack of hostility toward China; the widely expected hawkishness has not materialised.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: Lower probability of escalatory US tariffs/tech controls on China than consensus priced at term start; supportive for China-exposed risk assets.
insights.quote: The most surprising feature of his second term has been the lack of hostility towards the People’s Republic.

insights.claim: Trump and Xi Jinping are scheduled to hold their third bilateral meeting of the year on APEC's sidelines in Shenzhen, with the key question whether the 'constructive strategic stability' formulation holds or Trump applies more pressure.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: A key catalyst for US–China trade and tech-policy expectations; watch the communique language.

insights.claim: Bisley judges it unlikely Trump will use the summit to ramp up pressure on Xi, since his leader-level style is solicitous — the February 2025 Zelenskyy meeting being the notable exception.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: Base case is a friendly Trump–Xi meeting; downside surprise would be a genuine pivot.

insights.claim: If the US–China thaw is the prelude to a 'grand bargain', the consequences for the Asian regional order would be immense, reshaping allies' and neutrals' positions.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: A grand bargain would reprice Taiwan, Japan, Korea and ASEAN geopolitical risk and alliance-dependent defence spending.
insights.quote: if this is the prelude to a “grand bargain” then the regional consequences would be immense

insights.claim: The White House has trailed a Russia–China–US trilateral meeting to broker an end to the Ukraine war, styled as a 21st-century Yalta.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: Headline risk for European defence, energy and Ukraine-reconstruction trades.

insights.claim: An arrangement that includes Russia but not Ukraine is implausible as a lasting settlement, or indeed any peace at all.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: Fade rallies premised on a great-power-brokered Ukraine peace; conflict risk premium likely persists.
insights.quote: it is implausible that an arrangement including Russia and not involving Ukraine would create a lasting settlement

themes.theme: ASEAN/EAS agenda and Asian multilateralism under strain

insights.claim: APEC's trade-liberalisation business will remain peripheral to geopolitics at the summit, highlighting the misalignment between its liberal ideals and regional rivalry.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: Don't expect substantive trade liberalisation outcomes from APEC.

insights.claim: Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim's meeting with Myanmar junta leader Min Aung Hlaing may presage ASEAN bringing the military regime in from the cold.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: Normalisation of Myanmar's junta could reopen investment/trade channels but carries sanctions/reputational risk.

insights.claim: India and Indonesia are using the East Asia Summit to advance more ambitious global postures while carving out space between the US and China.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: Hedging middle powers are beneficiaries of supply-chain diversification.

insights.claim: ASEAN's major concerns going into the summits include energy prices, AI governance and maritime security.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: Energy prices are a live macro concern for ASEAN governments.

insights.claim: Sino-American competition has severely constrained Asian multilateral groupings' ability to build trust, and the summit season is unlikely to restore a more optimistic period.
insights.speaker: Nick Bisley
insights.so_what: Low expectations for multilateral breakthroughs; regional fragmentation persists.
